actions.heading: What to do first, and why
paragraphs: Grant the census key read access on the refused buckets, starting with the largest at {F146} hours. This is the single step that most reduces uncertainty in the {F130}-hour forecast.

Next, complete the samples of readable folders and shares and commission human checks on the model readings. Only then reprice tiering and confirm duplicates by hash. Keep pilot approval, preparation funding and destructive execution as separate decisions, each with an owner and an evidence gate.

chapter1.heading: The whole-estate forecast and its interval
paragraphs: The most likely holding is {F130} hours of media, with {F131} hours of speech ({K030}) and {F132} hours of music ({K031}). Speech and music are separate estimators over separate sampled windows and need not add to the total. The forecast covers every listed folder, refused and unsampled stores included. Forecast intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error.

The object store accounts for {F135} forecast hours and the file shares for {F137}. Only {F133} of the hours rest on files read and judged. The tables beside show the evidence basis and each bucket and share, with its ninety-five per cent forecast interval.

chapter2.heading: Languages, stores and text as assets
paragraphs: Speech sits mainly in the object store ({F136} forecast hours) rather than the file shares ({F138}), and {F140} of the object-store speech lies in buckets the key cannot read. The folder table beside shows the largest folders; it is a subset, not a complete folder schedule.

The written word is a separate, measured asset: {F080} live scripts, {F086} distinct texts, and script text whose size in millions of characters is {F084}, with {F085} of rows revisions. The workbench adds {F090} recordings and {F092} segments. Station broadcast language is not a script-level reading, and the inventories are not added together.

chapter3.heading: Where the hours, bytes and holding costs sit
paragraphs: The largest bucket carries {F146} forecast hours, {K033} of the estate, in {F038} TiB. Beyond it, {F036} TiB across {F037} buckets has not been written for over a year, and {F034} TiB are duplicate candidates matched on size and fingerprint. Candidates are not confirmed copies.

The tables beside name the buckets, tables and shares under review. The {F042} file shares hold {F041} files, but only sizes and dates were recorded, so duplication across channel shares is not measured. In the databases, {F004} GiB sit in {F002} tables, almost all in the largest databases ({K002}).

chapter4.heading: Work that converts forecast into measurement
paragraphs: The work is ordered by forecast exposure. First, an object-read grant on the {F104} refused buckets, which sit among the buckets holding {F139} forecast hours. Second, a restore decision on the {F105} archive-class buckets. Third, completing the planned samples, starting with the {F141} forecast hours in readable folders not yet sampled. Fourth, human checks on the model readings. Fifth, de-identifying selected product inputs.
The coverage and donor tables beside show what each step replaces. This work improves confidence and usability and is not a reason to withhold the estate forecast.

chapter6.heading: The decisions, in order
paragraphs: The decision table beside lists each decision with its source, destination or rule, responsible role and expected benefit, with money stated as an upper bound. The order matters. Access comes first because {F134} of the forecast depends on it. A restore decision, a pilot and its owner follow. Validation of tiering and duplicates comes before any move or deletion.
The model-roles table discloses how this pack was produced. Nothing described here has been executed; every destination is a proposal for approval.

compare.heading: Earn and save, side by side
paragraphs: Archive tiering addresses {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month. Duplicate reconciliation addresses {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O2.monthly_saving_usd} USD. Table tiering addresses {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB at up to {O3.monthly_saving_usd} USD. The legacy scenario total of {F019} USD is an upper bound, not verified net savings, and opportunities may overlap.

In the subset with recorded storage classes, {F114} of bytes are already archive-class, and those have no Standard-to-Archive saving left. Reprice eligible Standard bytes, with retrieval and restore costs, before relying on any figure.

On the earning side, {F018} database-derived candidates exist, each needing de-identification or aggregation. A speech-and-text pilot from the leading languages is a proposal, with no revenue evidence yet, and needs buyer validation.

exhibit_S002.heading: Database condition and the preparation queue
paragraphs: On measured and sampled rows, exact duplicates are {F007}, degraded rows {F008} and rows with empty required-looking fields {F009}. The last is a flag for review, not proof that every blank is invalid. {F010} of {F011} sampled rows carry personal-data markers, so de-identification or aggregation is a preparation step for any product.
Beyond rows, {F015} tables are empty, {F014} table pairs duplicate each other and dead columns are {F017} of measured columns. This is a bounded queue and does not reopen rights.

exhibit_S003.heading: Scale of the storage strategies
paragraphs: The three largest strategies address {F020} GiB of the {F021} GiB that all cost strategies reach. Archive tiering is the largest, at {O1.reclaimable_gib} GiB, then duplicate reconciliation at {O2.reclaimable_gib} GiB. Database tables not written for a year add {O3.reclaimable_gib} GiB, and database reclaimable bytes before pricing are {F005} GiB.
These are bytes addressed, not bytes deleted. Strategies overlap, and duplicate candidates are not safe to remove until confirmed by content hash.

exhibit_S004.heading: Estate bytes by store
paragraphs: The estate holds {F050} TiB. The object store is {F030} TiB ({K005}), the file shares {F040} TiB ({K006}) and the databases {F052} TiB ({K007}). Bytes are not invoice cost, and rounding means the stores may not reconcile exactly.
Media-store economics therefore deserve attention before database housekeeping. Database work is still worth doing for data condition and personal-data preparation, but it will not move storage cost.

exhibit_S005.heading: Byte concentration in the object store
paragraphs: The largest bucket holds {F038} TiB, {K008} of the {F030} TiB object store, and each of the next seven buckets is cold. These bytes are measured. What the largest bucket holds in hours, speech and languages is forecast, because it refuses object reads.
Concentration shows where to look first, not what it is worth. Storage volume establishes neither content quality nor revenue; the preparation chapter sets out the work that would.

exhibit_S010.heading: The staged corpus as a calibration sample
paragraphs: The staged corpus holds {F060} hours in {F063} files. Once music is set aside, {F061} hours are speech and {F062} hours are music, and {F074} files are mostly music. Read by both GPUs in {F067} GPU-hours, {F072} of judged windows agree with the folder language and the model declined to label {F066}.

The text model read {F070} transcripts, of which {F071} of passages agree with the folder language; {F075} were not reached. Window agreement is lowest in the Kikamba folder. This corpus is the natural base for human calibration of the estate-wide readings.

exhibit_S022.heading: Readable and unreadable media files
paragraphs: The census has listed {F100} media files in the object store and the file shares. In the object store, {F101} are in readable buckets and {F102} ({F103} TiB) are in buckets that refuse reads or need a restore. That is {F113} of listed object-store media files. {F104} buckets refuse object reads and {F105} need a restore.
A grant alone does not complete measurement; the census must then probe and sample those files. Egress so far is {F111} USD at an assumed tariff, and restores will add a retrieval fee not yet priced.

exhibit_S030.heading: How each forecast hour is known
paragraphs: The chart splits the estate forecast by evidence basis. {F147} hours were measured directly from folders read and judged. The largest block, {F139} hours, sits in buckets the key cannot read, and a further {F141} hours lie in readable folders not yet sampled. These medians are reported separately and are not an exactly additive stack.

The forecast rests on {F143} donor folders read and judged, {F144} files read in full, and {F145} simulations over {F142} folder strata. The forecast-to-measured ratio is {K034}. Each basis in the table beside names the single step that turns it into measurement.

exhibit_S031.heading: Seven languages, ranked by forecast speech hours
paragraphs: The estate is forecast to hold {F150} hours of Kiswahili speech, {F151} of Gikuyu, {F152} of Ekegusii, {F153} of Kalenjin, {F154} of Luo, {F155} of Wanga and {F156} of Kikamba. Kiswahili and Kikamba carry wide intervals relative to their medians.

In the readable scope alone Gikuyu leads Kiswahili. The forecast reverses the order because refused folders borrow from donors, and the two intervals overlap, so first place is not settled. These are model forecasts, not a human-certified language count.

exhibit_S032.heading: Where the forecast hours concentrate
paragraphs: Six of the ten largest folders or buckets by forecast hours are refused to the census key, so their hours are forecast from donors. The largest, at {F146} hours, is {K033} of the estate. The four readable entries among the ten are measured, with header probes and sampled content readings.

The owner should read this as a targeting rule. Reading the dominant refused bucket would convert {K033} of the estate forecast into measurement, and would remove the widest single interval from the total. Volume alone is not commercial value.

risks.heading: What the evidence cannot yet establish
paragraphs: The forecast of {F130} hours rests on donors, with {F133} of hours directly judged. It assumes refused buckets resemble readable folders of the same media kind and file size; if not, the truth lies outside the interval. Speech, music and language figures are model readings with sampling intervals only.

Savings, file-share duplication, script language, workbench overlap and buyer demand are also unmeasured. Each gap names its closing step: an access grant, human checks, class and demand data, fingerprinting, a text pass, a hash join or buyer review.

summary: RMS holds a large multilingual speech and text archive. Scaling what the census read in every folder to every listed folder, the estate most likely holds {F130} hours of media: {F131} hours of speech and {F132} hours of music, estimated separately and not an exact split. The ninety-five per cent forecast interval spans {F148} hours, {K032} of the forecast. Measured bytes are {F050} TiB. Only {F133} of the forecast hours rest on files read and judged, and {F134} sit in buckets the census key cannot read.

The strongest assets are the languages and the text. Kiswahili ({F150} speech hours), Gikuyu ({F151}) and Ekegusii ({F152}) lead the forecast, and the news archive adds {F080} live scripts. Value concentrates: one bucket the key cannot read carries {F146} forecast hours, {K033} of the estate, while the databases are {K007} of the bytes.

Preparation is work to do, not a reason to wait: object-read access, a restore decision, finishing the samples, checking the model readings and de-identifying product inputs. The first money path is repricing archive tiering, an upper bound of {O1.monthly_saving_usd} USD a month at legacy reference prices, followed by a speech-and-text pilot. Management is asked to decide access first.
